transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-11
Start time: 10:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Gomez (Redwood CSM), Maya Rodriguez (Bluefin Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Bluefin SRE), Priya Nair (Bluefin PM)
---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — follow up on the reliability incident from last week, go over the logs Samir sent, confirm mitigations and next steps. Maya, do you want to start with a quick recap from your side?
[00:22] Maya: Sure, yeah, thanks. So we saw a spike in 5xxs during our ramp on Friday around 14:05 UTC, it lasted about 7 to 10 minutes and manifested as timeouts and 503s from the Redwood endpoint. We were running the default SDK with parallelism of 40 and retries off initially to isolate the behavior.
[00:45] Carlos: yeah, and to add, Datadog shows p95 holding ok but p99 shot up and then a lot of queued requests. We also saw connection resets in the model server logs.
[01:10] Samir: Got it. I reviewed the server logs and there are a few patterns — 1) we saw model-worker OOMs on one backend host when large batches were accepted, 2) there were transient 502/503 responses from the proxy layer when the worker restarted, and 3) we detected a retry stampede on the client side when the first wave hit failures.
[01:40] Priya: Retry stampede meaning the client retried too quickly and amplified load?
[01:46] Samir: Exactly yeah, no jitter and hard retry count of 5 caused waves. Also our batching settings allowed very large batch sizes during the ramp which pushed memory.
[02:10] Avery: So short-term, what did you test as mitigations? I remember we temporarily disabled parallelism down to 8 and reduced max batch size?
[02:20] Maya: Right, we dropped parallelism and re-ran. The 5xxs didn't come back at the same scale, but p99 latency still higher than target. We also tried a client-side exponential backoff with jitter and that helped smoothing.
[02:41] Samir: I pushed a patch on the runtime side to fail fast when queue depth exceeds threshold — that keeps the proxy from queuing too many requests and causing head-of-line blocking. But that results in earlier 429s unless we do capacity reservation.
[03:05] Carlos: 429s are preferable to long tail 5xxs in our view, at least they are explicit rate signals. We can handle 429s with backoff.
[03:18] Leah: Quick note — Redwood can also provision a small dedicated pool for your pilot to avoid noisy neighbors while you tune. That is an option we can price out.
[03:30] Priya: That may help. For the pilot we want predictable latency more than lowest cost.
[03:38] Avery: Okay noted. Samir, can you share the annotated logs you mentioned? The last email had raw logs but not the timeline mapping to Datadog traces.
[03:49] Samir: Yep, I will. I have a timeline with host IDs, timestamps, and worker restarts. I'll annotate with the matching Datadog span IDs. Expect that by EOD tomorrow.
[04:00] Maya: One question — are those OOMs caused by the model variant memory profile or by batch sizing?
[04:08] Samir: A combination. The variant you're using is quantized and memory-friendlier, but with extreme batch sizes and long max sequence length we still see memory spikes. The runtime's kernel selection currently favors throughput which can increase peak mem. We can force a memory-optimized kernel for those hosts.
[04:31] Carlos: Is that kernel switch something we do on our side or Redwood does it?
[04:36] Samir: Redwood runtime change, but we can coordinate to flip it for your pilot nodes and monitor. No code changes required from you.
[04:44] Priya: That would be great. Also curiosity — does the Redwood SDK expose better defaults for retries/backoff? We didn't realize the defaults would amplify the issue.
[04:55] Avery: Good callout. We'll share a recommended SDK config for pilots that sets conservative parallelism, jittered backoff and a max concurrency. Samir will include the snippet.
[05:09] Maya: ok thanks. Also, is there a way to get per-route rate limits so we can avoid shared quota issues when other teams run tests?
[05:18] Leah: Yes, per-route quotas are supported on Dedicated and on hosted we can add route-level throttles. For production you'd probably want dedicated to guarantee throughput.
[05:29] Carlos: For now a hosted route throttle would help.
[05:33] Samir: Quick technical detail — we also observed KV cache cold misses at the start of the ramp which increased per-token work. Warming the prefix cache helped reduce tokens processed and smoothed latency.
[05:50] Maya: That matches our perf traces. We have some prompt variations that prevent cache hits. We will try to standardize prompts where possible.
[05:59] Priya: Anything else in the runtime we should be aware of?
[06:04] Samir: We have a circuit breaker feature that proactively rejects requests when queue depth or error rate crosses a threshold; it's disabled by default but we can enable it for your pilot to prevent cascading failures.
[06:16] Carlos: We'd like that on as an experiment. What's the expected client experience? 429s or 503s?
[06:22] Samir: Circuit breaker returns 429s and includes a Retry-After header. Works better with client-side backoff.
[06:29] Avery: Ok we'll recommend the combination: enable circuit breaker, set client retries with jitter and cap concurrency.
[06:36] Maya: On the monitoring side, Carlos will share Datadog links. Will Redwood be able to ingest traces or do we just exchange span IDs?
[06:46] Samir: We don't ingest them directly. Best is to share trace links and span IDs; we'll correlate with server logs. We can also send a short instruction on what traces to collect.
[06:55] Carlos: I'll export the top traces around 14:00-14:20 UTC on 2026-05-09.
[07:00] Priya: timelines and owners are helpful.
[07:04] Avery: Let's step through concrete root-cause hypotheses so the action items are clear. Hypothesis A: client-side retry storm amplifies transient failures. Hypothesis B: large batch sizes + long seqs cause worker OOMs. Hypothesis C: cold KV cache increases per-token work and latency. Are we all aligned?
[07:25] Maya: Yes. That sounds right.
[07:28] Samir: Agreed. We also have Hypothesis D: autoscaler timing — if pods spin up slowly under burst, the proxy's queue grows which can cause proxy-level timeouts.
[07:40] Carlos: That one resonated — we saw scale events in k8s around the same time.
[07:46] Priya: For mitigation, short-term we prefer SDK config + circuit breaker + smaller batch sizes. Mid-term: dedicated pool and kernel switch. Long-term: autoscale tuning and maybe a warmup job for cache.
[08:04] Samir: We'll prepare an experiment plan: 1) Apply conservative SDK config and enable circuit breaker, 2) run a targeted ramp to reproduce, 3) if issues persist, flip memory-optimized kernel on pilot hosts, 4) run an instrumented load test.
[08:22] Avery: Sounds good. Maya, are there any business constraints we should be aware of — e.g., timeline to decision, stakeholders?
[08:30] Maya: We're on a 6-week pilot path. Decision around dedicated vs hosted will be influenced by latency SLOs in week 4. Stakeholders: me, Carlos, Priya and infra leads.
[08:43] Leah: We'll make sure the pricing/committed pool options are in the follow-up.
[08:48] Carlos: A couple of specific asks — can Redwood instrument request IDs so we can map client request id -> server logs more easily? Right now correlation is manual.
[08:58] Samir: We include request_id in server logs if the client sends a request_id header. If you can add that header in the SDK calls we can do exact matching. I'll include the header snippet.
[09:11] Priya: Great. Also curious on the retry policy — does Redwood recommend total retry attempts and max elapsed time?
[09:18] Samir: For pilots we recommend max_attempts=3, base_delay=200ms, jitter, and total max elapsed ~2-3s depending on your latency tolerance. We'll put recommended values in the doc.
[09:33] Maya: ok thanks.
[09:36] Avery: Anything else folks want to surface?
[09:39] Carlos: One oddity — we saw increased 5xxs when another team ran long-running evals. Could be noisy neighbor effect. That would point to dedicated pool being the right long-term move.
[09:51] Leah: We'll get you a price example for a small dedicated pool for the pilot and also share burst options.
[09:58] Priya: On data security — SSO/SCIM questions remain for our enterprise review but not urgent for the pilot.
[10:06] Avery: We'll include the security docs link in the email follow-up.
[10:10] Maya: ok perfect.
[10:13] Avery: Quick recap of next steps: Samir to share annotated logs + header snippet, Redwood to provide SDK recommended config and retry doc, Bluefin to share Datadog traces, Redwood to run targeted load test and share results, Avery to send pricing/DED options. We'll reconvene after the log handoff and load test.
[10:34] Maya: sounds good thanks everyone.
[10:36] Avery: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
